newsitem.title: USA: LDC debt joins U.S. Treasuries in relief rally.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt joins U.S. Treasuries in relief rally.

text.p: Emerging market debt rose in dealer-driven trading on Thursday as volatility in U.S. Treasuries kept retail investors out of the market, traders said.
"There hasn't been retail involvement in the market to speak of all week," one head Brady trader said. "It's been mainly a dealer- and trading account-dominated market."
Emerging debt prices climbed in tandem with Treasuries as a string of key U.S. economic reports finally ended, traders said.
U.S. data Wednesday on consumer inflation, industrial production and business inventories largely reflected economists' forecasts, sparking a relief rally, they said.
Yield spreads narrowed for most emerging issues. Mexico saw particularly strong professional demand, traders said.
On Thursday morning, Mexico reported a surprisingly strong 9.9-percent surge in industrial production for June, adding to a brightening macroeconomic picture in the country.
"They definitely came out stronger than what we were looking for, but that just emphasizes the Street's view on Mexico," one trader said.
Mexico's UMS 2026 global bonds climbed 1-1/2 to 122-1/8, tightening about seven basis points.
Brazil "C" bonds rose a full point to 84-1/8, while Argentina FRBs edged 1/8 higher to 95-3/4.
Traders said the lack of retail involvement may eventually erode the spread tightening of the last few sessions.

"The bonds are just getting passed around the Street," one trader said. "Generally when you have something like that and you get a gap in Treasuries, it means we're going to give it all up in terms of spread."
Prefacing Thursday's gains, the U.S. Labor Department reported its Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.2 percent both overall and in its core components in July, exactly matching experts' forecasts.
Forty-five minutes later, the Federal Reserve said U.S. industrial production climbed 0.2 percent while capacity utilization fell slightly to 83.1 percent, coming very close to projections.
